description: JVM primitive arrays slice (ISSUE-0094). JVM-only fixtures (plus seven cross-backend parity fixtures that also run under LuaJIT as the reference) that run the real DEAL frontend (lexer → parser → name resolver → type checker) → real JvmBackend codegen → javac subprocess → java subprocess executing the emitted artifact (the harness fails a fixture whose codegen or JVM execution is bypassed). Covered forms: int[]/number[]/string[]/boolean[] array literals (including the empty literal under a contextual type), index reads, element writes (in-place writes, the i === length append — via the xs[xs.length] idiom and via a plain index-equals-length write — with the wrapped storage growing in place so aliases observe every write), .length reads, arrays through function parameters and returns, runtime bounds checks (negative read → E8002, read past the end → E8001 "expected int, got null" mirroring LuaJIT's nil-at-the-boundary, negative write → E8002, gap write → E8002, out-of-safe-range int element write → E8004 via the element value check), spec §Operational semantics evaluation order for reads (receiver before index) and writes (receiver, index, RHS before the LHS write check — including hoisted null-typed side effects materialized into temporaries in order, and the side-effecting receiver + hoisting index + hoisting RHS shape anchored at the earliest hoist start after each operand), array-literal element evaluation order with a side-effecting first element and hoisting later elements, === / !== operand positions for past-end reads in all four element types (nil comparison semantics per the spec read-site contract, never E8001), negative indexes in comparison positions (E8002 on both backends), and two frontend compile-error gates rejected before any backend (E3007 non-int index, E3017 read-only .length assignment).

tests.name: jvm-arr-literal-read-length
tests.description: An int[] literal, index reads, and .length: xs[0]+xs[1]+xs[2]+xs.length computes 63 (10+20+30+3) through the real frontend → JvmBackend codegen → javac → java artifact execution

tests.name: jvm-arr-write-readback
tests.description: Element writes into existing indexes mutate the array in place: xs[1] = 99, then xs[2] = xs[0] + xs[1] (=100), and the sum reads back 200

tests.name: jvm-arr-append-at-length
tests.description: Writing at i === length appends (spec §Array writes): an empty literal grows via the xs[xs.length] = v append idiom (0→1→2) and a plain index-equals-length write appends the third element; the final sum + length is 10

tests.name: jvm-arr-four-element-types
tests.description: number[], string[], and boolean[] literals, writes, reads, and length all run end-to-end: ns[1] recomputed to 2.5, ss[0] set to ss[1] + "x" = "bx", bs[1] set to bs[0] = true, every length reads 2

tests.name: jvm-arr-function-param-return
tests.description: Arrays flow through function parameters and returns: fill(xs, 10) writes xs[0]=10 and xs[1]=11 into the caller's array and returns it, total(ys) sums 21, + xs.length = 23

tests.name: jvm-arr-alias-mutation-append
tests.description: Array aliases share one mutable wrapper: b = a, then b[1] = 9 and the b[3] = 4 append are both observed through a (a[1] + a[3] + a.length = 9 + 4 + 4 = 17) — append grows the wrapped storage in place, so the alias identity is stable

tests.name: jvm-arr-negative-read-e8002
tests.description: A negative index read is a runtime E8002 (LuaJIT's emitted negative-array-index check), exit 1 — the read helper performs the bounds check before touching the storage

tests.name: jvm-arr-oob-read-e8001
tests.description: A read past the end is a runtime E8001 "expected int, got null" (spec §Bounds and nil behavior: LuaJIT reads nil there and the read site's typed boundary fails with that shape) — the JVM read raises the boundary failure directly, exit 1

tests.name: jvm-arr-negative-write-e8002
tests.description: A negative index write is a runtime E8002 (spec §Array writes rule 5: i < 0 is a runtime error), exit 1

tests.name: jvm-arr-gap-write-e8002
tests.description: Writing past the end with a gap (i > length) is a runtime E8002 (spec §Array writes rule 5) — only i === length appends, exit 1

tests.name: jvm-arr-eval-order-read
tests.description: Read evaluation order (spec §Operational semantics rule 1): the receiver expression runs before the index expression — get prints 'arr', mark prints 'idx', then the read returns xs[2] = 300

tests.name: jvm-arr-eval-order-write
tests.description: Write evaluation order (spec §Operational semantics rule 3: the assignment RHS evaluates before the LHS write check): receiver 'arr', index 'idx', RHS 'rhs' run strictly left to right, then the bounds check + store write xs[0] = 42

tests.name: jvm-arr-eval-order-hoisted
tests.description: Left-to-right order survives hoisted null-typed side effects in the index and RHS: the index operand's hoisted 'index-side' print runs before its inline pick('index') call, which is materialized into a temporary ahead of the RHS's hoisted 'value-side' print — output index-side, index, value-side, value, then the written xs[0] = 0

tests.name: jvm-arr-eval-order-write-hoisted-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for write evaluation order with a side-effecting receiver and hoisting index and RHS operands: getArr prints 'a' (receiver first, spec §Operational semantics rule 1+3), the index operand's hoisted print 'b' runs before its inline pick('i') call, which is materialized into a temporary ahead of the RHS's hoisted print 'c', then pick('v') and the write — a, b, i, c, v, write-ok under both real luajit and the emitted JVM artifact (LuaJIT agrees on this shape)
tests.expectedOutput:
a
b
i
c
v
write-ok

tests.name: jvm-arr-literal-eval-order-hoisted-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for array-literal element evaluation order with a side-effecting first element and hoisting later elements: getA prints 'a' before the second element's hoisted print 'b', its inline pick('i') call is materialized into a temporary ahead of the third element's hoisted print 'c', then pick('v') — a, b, i, c, v, lit-ok under both real luajit and the emitted JVM artifact
tests.expectedOutput:
a
b
i
c
v
lit-ok

tests.name: jvm-arr-cmp-past-end-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity for === / !== with array reads past the end in all four element types: the read site applies no typed boundary at a comparison operand (spec §Bounds and nil behavior), so LuaJIT reads nil and computes the comparison — xs[99] === 5 is false, xs[99] !== 5 is true, xs[99] === xs[99] is true (nil === nil), and the same nil semantics hold for number[]/string[]/boolean[] reads. The JVM emits boxed reads that yield null past the end instead of raising E8001, so both backends print int-neq, nil-eq-nil, number-neq, string-neq, boolean-neq, mixed
tests.expectedOutput:
int-neq
nil-eq-nil
number-neq
string-neq
boolean-neq
mixed

tests.name: jvm-arr-cmp-negative-index-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity: a negative array index in a comparison operand still raises E8002 on both backends — LuaJIT emits the negative-index check unconditionally at the read, whatever the surrounding position, and the JVM boxed comparison read raises it the same way (exit 1 on both)

tests.name: jvm-arr-frontend-reject-index-type
tests.description: A non-int array index is rejected by the frontend type checker (E3007 Array index must be int) before any backend runs — codegen/javac/java never invoked

tests.name: jvm-arr-frontend-reject-length-write
tests.description: Assignment to the read-only array .length intrinsic is rejected by the frontend type checker (E3017 Array length is read-only) before any backend runs — codegen/javac/java never invoked

tests.name: jvm-arr-literal-read-write-length-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity: int[] literal, element writes, the xs[xs.length] append idiom, .length, and alias mutation produce identical observable results under LuaJIT (the reference) and the emitted JVM artifact — every assertion routed through console output

tests.name: jvm-arr-multi-type-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity: number[]/string[]/boolean[] literals, writes, and reads produce identical observable results under LuaJIT and the emitted JVM artifact

tests.name: jvm-arr-negative-read-parity
tests.description: Cross-backend parity: the negative index read raises E8002 on both LuaJIT (its emitted negative-index check) and the emitted JVM artifact, exit 1 on both
